feature: op6893 21651: modem resource owners, cold power cycle and SCP READY1 on the new unit

images.purpose: cold platform owner; first probe failed -EBUSY with both handoff owners enabled
cold power cycle verified after disabling the metadata-only node
SCP runtime, MD prepare/release, FS/RPC services
kernel RPC 0x4009 answered with the audited MD-view numbers; MD passes mml1_rf but asserts on the 0x0f fill
band-support straps sampled at probe from band-strap-gpios/band-strap-ids

lk_handoff.record: version=3 tags=20 bytes=2664 ccb=1; modem not started
lk_handoff.note: 21651 runs 20615's LK, so the mblock addresses match; the cached bank is 0x8a000000+0x2960000 here rather than the 0x88000000+0x4960000 the board file declares, and the driver uses LK's value

exclusive_owner.problem: with both modem-handoff and modem-platform enabled the platform probe failed: LK metadata inspection failed: stage=snapshot error=-16
exclusive_owner.cause: only one owner may snapshot the LK tag buffer; the second memremap-backed read is refused

cold_power_cycle.note: the platform owner never changes voltages and never releases the MD CPU

scp.runtime: active=1 ready=1 generation=1 events=2 ready_channel=22 awake_pairs=1 error=0 cleanup_error=0
scp.observation: selector=0 gated=0 firmware_base=0x9fa00000 firmware_size=0x500000 share_base=0x8d000000 share_size=0x320000
scp.stop: active=0 generation=0, awake_fault=1 recorded because the paired awake put raced the deliberate SCP stop

first_attempt.result: MD asserted: ex_type=80 (ASSERT_FAIL_EXCEPTION) line=3414 path=mcu/service/nvram/src/nvram_main.c para=0x0,0x20,0x0
first_attempt.conclusion: the migration notes say not to reuse 20615 private data; the 21651 NVRAM is a different snapshot

second_attempt.nvram_source: 21651's own partitions, read-only from mainline: Z<-nvdata/md X<-protect1/md Y<-protect2/md S<-nvcfg, 452 files
second_attempt.result: the nvram_main assert is gone; the MD consumed 727 FS replies and then asserted in mcu/driver/ccismcore/src/ccismcore_ccci.c line=2031 para=0x4,0x9eeca80,0x0
second_attempt.backend: stopped with UnsupportedOperation while decoding a reply schema
second_attempt.conclusion: the vendor's NVRAM backup rotation (find + Move of the FILELIST files) is not modelled; the MD asserts in CCISM after the FS error

md1img.note: the version string matches 20615 but the partition SHA-256 differs between the units, so it is a different build of the same release

items: the modem tree enables the PMIC supplies, MD1 domain, modem-platform, SCP owner/observe and DPMAIF, and disables modem-handoff
the smem_clear policy attribute now follows CONFIG_OP6893_CCCI_MD_BOOT, which fixes the link failure when the platform owner is built without the boot owner

pre_existing_test_failure.note: the committed driver calls memcpy_fromio/memcpy_toio/memset_io in the TCM restore path, so the test's 'no I/O' expectation is stale; unrelated to this change

fs_semantics.conclusion: wide path arguments are NUL-terminated C strings; the MD reuses its buffers
fs_semantics.observed: Move destination carried the previous FindFirst pattern 'Z:\NVRAM\BACKUP\FILE*' after the terminator, which the vendor ignores and the backend rejected with -16
fs_semantics.delete: 0x100f is FS_CCCI_Delete: one wide path, unlink of one regular file, mapped errno on failure; a directory returns the generic -18 as the vendor's unlink does
fs_semantics.unsupported_rpc: an unimplemented user RPC now answers the vendor's single s32 NO_OP=-1 instead of failing the whole submit

gpio_adc_0x4009.owner: kernel; ccci_rpc_owner() classifies every id except 0x400f/0x4010 as CCCI_RPC_KERNEL, so a userspace handler is never reached
gpio_adc_0x4009.request: 425-byte v2 record, reqMask=3, gpioValidPinMask=0x000f, names starting GPIO_FDD_Band_Support_Detection_*
gpio_adc_0x4009.straps: band-strap-gpios = <&pio 63..66>, band-strap-ids = <63 64 65 66>, sampled once at probe
gpio_adc_0x4009.measured_levels: 63=1 64=0 65=1 66=0, read on this unit with the GPIO v2 character device (GPIO_V2_GET_LINE_IOCTL + GET_VALUES), not inferred
gpio_adc_0x4009.corroboration: /data/src/frog/1.log (project 21609) shows the same 1,0,1,0 pattern; used only as a cross-check
gpio_adc_0x4009.before: status 0 with the vendor's 0x0f fill everywhere, MD asserted in mcu/l1/mml1/mml1_rf/src/mmrf/gen97/mml1_rf_error_check.c:211 para=0x1,0xf0f0f0f

hs2_blocker.state: HS1 accepted, runtime published, WAIT_HS2; the MD spends 40-50 s and about 6000 FS requests in its early NVRAM pass, then asserts
hs2_blocker.ccism: state=1 (ARMED) md_open=1 scp_open=1; the vendor sends CCISM_SHM_INIT only after MD READY, so ARMED is a consequence
hs2_blocker.md_ee: version=0xab000005 cores=12 offender=MCU ex_type=80 class=assert line=2031 path=mcu/driver/ccismcore/src/ccismcore_ccci.c para=0x4,0x9eeca80,0x0 lr=0x90103244
excluded: runtime feature set: the tree already grants the 28 features that unblocked 20615
feature 15: runtime_mask=0x8000 leaves both the negotiated table and the assert unchanged
userspace latency: respond() measures 0.13-0.20 ms per request on the device; tracing on/off changes the request count by 2%
FS semantics: the rotation, Restore, CMPT and attribute paths all progress until the MD itself asserts
hs2_blocker.needed: MD-side observability (DFD log or the ccismcore param meaning); further AP-side guesses have no evidence behind them
